name: Quick Mart PLC
unit: KES, printed in thousands (KES '000) and stored absolute (x1000 = whole Kenya Shillings)
scale_note: Source memorandum states all figures in KES '000; multiplied by 1000 here, the same whole-currency unit the other statement files use.
listing_status: Not listed. Offer for sale 05-30 October 2026; listing and commencement of trading 12 November 2026. No traded price, no market capitalisation, no traded P/E exist.
source: Quick Mart PLC Information Memorandum, Initial Public Offering, 02 October 2026. Historical and interim figures from the Reporting Accountants Report, 'Selected Historical Financial Information' (page marker 119 / printed 117, profit or loss; marker 121 / printed 119, financial position; marker 122 / printed 120, cash flow). Projected figures from the memorandum's own table headed 'Projected' (marker 138 / printed 136) and the front valuation box (marker 32-33 / printed 30-31). The memorandum reports KES thousands; every value here is x1000 = whole Kenya Shillings. Not listed: the company has no traded price, no market capitalisation and no traded P/E, so none is recorded in these files.
projectionNote: No projection: the memorandum publishes a projected profit or loss, not a projected cash flow statement. Every column here is reported.

rows.note: Not a panel row. Excludes IFRS 16 lease interest.

rows.label: Working capital movement
rows.note: Not a panel row. In H1 2026 the shareholders' advance of KES 1.1bn was reclassified out of working capital movement into financing activities.

rows.label: Operating Cash Flow
rows.note: The memorandum's 'Net cash flows from operating activities'.

rows.label: Investing Cash Flow
rows.note: The memorandum's 'Net cash flows used in investing activities'; stored negative as printed.

rows.label: Financing Cash Flow
rows.note: The memorandum's 'Net cash flows used in financing activities'; stored negative as printed.

rows.label: Capital Expenditure
rows.source: not stated as a cash-flow line in the memorandum
rows.note: Withheld. The memorandum's cash flow statement carries no separate capital expenditure line; it gives purchases of property and equipment only as rounded prose (KES 1.2bn FY2021; 1.8bn FY2022; 865.5m FY2023; 393.5m FY2024; 1.1bn FY2025, marker 135 / printed 133), which is not exact to the unit and is not stored as a filed figure.

rows.label: Free Cash Flow
rows.note: Withheld: the memorandum does not print a free cash flow line and capex (its input) is not exact.

rows.label: Cash at Beginning of Period
rows.note: Not a panel row. The memorandum's 'Cash and equivalents at 1 January'.

rows.label: Cash at End of Period
rows.note: Not a panel row; the same figure appears as Cash & Equivalents in the balance sheet.

identityChecks: Operating Cash Flow + Investing Cash Flow + Financing Cash Flow = Net Change in Cash
Cash at Beginning of Period + Net Change in Cash = Cash at End of Period
reconciliation_note: Operating + Investing + Financing equals Net Change in Cash on every period. The H1 2026 operating line is stated on the memorandum's own re-based presentation (shareholders' advance reclassified to financing); it is a six-month figure and is not comparable to a full year without that note and the half-year length.
note: Capital Expenditure and Free Cash Flow are absent by design, not zero: the memorandum's selected statement of cash flow (marker 122 / printed 120) carries only cash generation before working capital, working capital movement, net cash from operating, investing and financing activities, the net movement in cash and the opening and closing balances. It prints no purchase-of-property-and-equipment line, so no capital expenditure figure can be read from the statement and none is recorded. The narrative (marker 135 / printed 133) describes investing outflows qualitatively and the capital-expenditure bar chart is given only to one significant figure, which is not enough to state a figure at the precision the panel prints. A dash here is honest; a rounded narrative number printed as a filed one would not be.
